subject: Observability hardening and bastion-mediated SIEM export for private deployment

Subject: Private observability export requirements and onboarding

Hi Marissa,

We're progressing on our private deployment evaluation and have a couple of non-negotiable requirements from our security team for telemetry exports: minimal egress, all outbound traffic must go through a bastion/proxy in our VPC, and strict IP allowlisting on the destination side. We also need proof of custody for logs (signed certificates, retention controls) for our SOC review.

I've attached the Helio ingress requirements doc for context. Can Redwood support a bastion-mediated export model where our forwarder posts logs/traces via TLS to a proxy in our VPC and Redwood pulls/ingests from that proxy? If not, what are recommended deployment patterns that satisfy our controls?

Thanks — I can join a technical call if easier.

Mike Reynolds
Head of Security Ops, HelioBank

On Tue, Sep 15, 2026 at 09:12 AM Mike Reynolds <mike.reynolds@heliobank.com> wrote:
> We're progressing on our private deployment evaluation and have a couple of non-negotiable requirements...

Hi all — technical summary and options:

1) Push-to-proxy (recommended for Helio constraints):
   - Customer runs a TLS-terminating proxy (bastion) in their VPC.
   - Forwarder inside customer network POSTs to proxy (HTTPS, mutual TLS optional).
   - Proxy forwards to a Redwood ingress endpoint that is allowlisted to only accept traffic from the proxy's egress IPs.
   - Benefits: no direct outbound from protected subnets, simple allowlist on our side, clear network boundary.

2) Pull-from-dropbox (alternate):
   - Customer places batched evidence (compressed logs/traces) in an SFTP/HTTPS bucket behind the bastion; Redwood fetches on schedule via an ephemeral tunnel.
   - Benefits: tight custody, easier for air-gapped workflows; tradeoff: latency and complexity.

3) Agent/Forwarder inside VPC with outbound via bastion SOCKS/TLS tunnel to Redwood HEC endpoint.

Tracing hooks: we can support OTLP over TLS to the same proxy; span IDs and timestamps preserved. We'll need to validate header pass-through and max-payload sizing for long traces.

Required artifacts from Helio for design + security sign-off:
- Network allowlist (CIDR / fixed egress IPs)
- TLS cert chain or mTLS config if they want mutual auth
- Example log payloads (sample size ~5MB) and schema (jsonlines)
- Expected retention and access pattern (who can pull)

I've opened OBS-3492 to track the technical work and preflight checks. I'll attach a short bastion config snippet that demonstrates our recommended ACLs.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Security/Privacy Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — that helps a lot. A few clarifying items from our auditors:

- Helio will operate a pair of bastion proxies (active/passive) with stable egress IPs. Will Redwood accept a short list (2 IPs per region) for src allowlisting?
- For custody and retention evidence: do you produce a signed evidence package (certificate of ingestion + retention policy) that we can add to our SOC artifact bundle?
- We also need to confirm that Redwood's ingest path preserves original timestamps and trace IDs and that any sampling is documented.

If you can confirm these three items we can move to scheduling the onboarding call and prepare procurement paperwork.

— Mike
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-17T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability export requirements and onboarding

Mike — good questions. Short answers and next steps:

1) Allowlisting: yes — we can accept a small set of egress IPs per region for the ingestion endpoints. We'll map the IPs to a fixed customer routing entry and validate in preflight.

2) Evidence bundle: Redwood will produce an ingestion certificate (signed), an evidence manifest listing ingested files/streams with timestamps, and a retention statement aligned to the selected retention tier. We can include a SOC-ready artifact pack for Helio's auditors.

3) Tracing and sampling: the default ingestion preserves timestamps and span/trace IDs. Any sampling will be configurable and documented in the rollout notes; by default sampling is disabled for onboarding runs so you get full fidelity for initial verification.

Deliverables we'll provide before the call:
- Helio onboarding checklist (attached)
- Preflight network test plan (we run test pushes and confirm egress IPs)
- Evidence bundle template and SOC artifact list
- Proposed 45m tech onboarding slot — link below to choose a time

Scheduling + links: https://cal.redwood.ai/teams/onboarding/45m, DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/templates/REDWOOD-ONBOARD-1

Please review the attached checklist and propose two windows this week for the call. We'll aim to have the preflight run within 48 hours of the call.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
